cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code constructs an OS command using string concatenation with external input (files parameter), which is the core mechanism of CWE-78

connection.evidence: Files parameter flows from commit function call to command execution, but external control is not established - files come from internal file processing of package.json paths

diff_causality.evidence: This is an added line (change_type: 'A'), but the counterfactual shows it's part of normal git workflow functionality rather than creating a vulnerability

security_control.evidence: The escapeQuotes function provides sanitization by escaping quotes and special characters, but effectiveness against all command injection vectors is unresolved
security_control.required_control: Proper neutralization of shell metacharacters in command arguments
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-78 requires neutralization of shell metacharacters when constructing commands from external input
existing_controls_checked: escapeQuotes function escapes quotes, dollar signs, backticks, and backslashes
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The escapeQuotes function provides some protection but may not cover all shell metacharacters or edge cases; using parameterized execution methods would be more robust

concrete_impact.evidence: Impact depends on whether malicious file paths can reach this code, which is unresolved - files appear to be from internal package.json processing

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the git add operation would be missing from the commit workflow, breaking normal functionality rather than removing a vulnerability.
supporting_evidence: Command construction uses string concatenation with external 'files' parameter
Uses child_process.exec which executes commands through the system shell
Files parameter flows through the commit function interface
contradicting_evidence: Files are sourced from internal file processing of package.json, not direct user input
escapeQuotes function provides sanitization against common injection characters
This is an added line implementing normal git workflow functionality
unresolved_facts: Whether file paths could contain malicious content from external sources
Effectiveness of escapeQuotes against all command injection vectors
Source and validation of files parameter before reaching commit function
review_comment: The code constructs git commands using string concatenation with file paths, but these paths appear to come from internal package.json processing rather than external user input. While the escapeQuotes function provides some protection, consider using child_process.execFile with separate arguments instead of shell execution for more robust security. Validate that file paths originate only from trusted internal sources before command construction.
